<b>Step 1 of 3 — Find context automatica:
Step 1 of 3 — Find context automatically (no AI)

Matches each non-empty game string to a marked script line by the text itself. Exact unique matches are saved at once. Repeated greetings and near-matches come back one by one below so you can Use Context, pick another place, or mark Not Story.

This has to finish before timeline or voices: those jobs only read linked lines. Re-run after you re-mark the script; already-decided links are kept unless the source text changed.
<b>Step 2 of 3 — Build the timeline (AI):
Step 2 of 3 — Build the timeline (AI)

Reads linked dialogue in story order and writes a short event for each stretch: where we are, what just happened, what the scene is about.

That package is what the translation prompt uses instead of “translate this sentence in isolation”. Midna after the children are taken is not the same Midna as in Ordon.

Needs step 1. Does not fill the glossary. Run it before the glossary describe pass if you want scene notes available there. Long and billed per chunk; already-analysed stretches are reused.

Grey until step 1 has produced at least one link.
<b>Step 3 of 3 — Analyse character voice:
Step 3 of 3 — Analyse character voices (AI)

Reads each named speaker’s linked lines and writes how they talk: register, tempo, habits, address (ти/ви), and translator guidance so Midna, Renado and a shop clerk do not share one voice.

Uses the names from Markup Studio / Merge Speakers. It does not invent or rename characters, and it does not dump a raw-script guess into the glossary.

Needs step 1. Best before glossary descriptions, so character notes can quote a real voice profile. Grey until step 1 has links.

<b>What this tab is for.</b> The game fi:
What this tab is for. The game file has lines; the marked script has story. Until they are linked, translation cannot know which scene a row belongs to.

Step 1 is automatic and does not use AI: it matches game text to marked dialogue. Clear matches are saved; only doubtful ones come back for a decision below. Menus and system messages are skipped.

Step 2 (timeline) and step 3 (voices) are the analysis. They need step 1 first. Run them before you fill glossary descriptions if you want those notes and the translation prompt to know what already happened and how the speaker talks. This is the story-context step of the localization pipeline — after the script is marked up and speakers are named, before the glossary is filled and the game text is translated.

First import the Markup Studio project. Then link each game line to its place in that script. Then, if you want scene-aware translation, ask the AI to write what already happened (timeline) and how each character speaks (voices). Glossary and translation read those results; they do not replace them.

This script has not been marked up in Script Markup Studio, so the speakers have to be guessed.

Guessing means every ALL-CAPS line is read as a name and everything under it as that character's lines. Section banners and shouted words become speakers, a heading that is not upper case is missed entirely, and stage directions blur into speech. Names will be wrong and many will not be found.
